A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Event2Vec by the same authors. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A.1–A.9 are readable and support a complete comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V4 reports original classification, throughput, latency, robustness, linear-probing, and ablation results across three neuromorphic datasets, including appendix experiments.

after.justification: V6 retains these original empirical results and adds comparisons within the transfer linear-probing experiment.

M1.justification: The core embeddings, density weighting, and FoX backbone remain. The specified temporal input changes from unnormalized forward differences with trailing zero padding to normalized backward differences with an initial zero. Appendix A.5 specifies masking spatial embeddings before fusion instead of replacing complete event tokens, and A.2 revises normalization from key/value to query/key projections. These are procedural specification changes; implementation changes are not independently established.

E1.justification: Both versions use DVS Gesture, ASL-DVS, and DVS-Lip for the same classification, pretraining, and transfer-probing coverage. Event-count and spatial-resolution stress scenarios are retained. The additional probing controls do not introduce another dataset or task.

E2.justification: V6 Table 3 adds raw-event and standard-spatial/sinusoidal-temporal comparators to the existing transfer-probing experiment, including comparisons without Transformer layers. External comparators in Tables 1–2 and the clustering comparison remain unchanged. The expanded EventNet discussion does not report an evaluated EventNet baseline.

E3.justification: Several consequential reported settings change. Table 1 revises ASL-DVS input from 512 to 1024 events. Appendix A.2 adds the per-GPU batch-size factor to learning-rate scaling, implying a 64-fold difference at the stated batch size, and narrows gradient-clipping coverage. Appendices A.5 and A.9 revise masking and augmentation specifications, including span-start probability and Gesture chunk dropout. Table 3 adds probing controls. These substantially revise the experimental recipe without establishing reruns.

E4.justification: The existing transfer-probing analysis is extended to separate raw-input separability, embedding contributions, and contributions from five Transformer layers, with proposed versus standard embeddings. The earlier embedding ablation, event-count and resolution robustness tests, clustering analysis, attention variants, and visual case studies remain.

E5.justification: Both versions specify mean and standard deviation reporting and 10 independent test runs for experiments involving random sampling. The added probing rows follow the existing uncertainty-reporting practice; no new seed policy, confidence intervals, or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: V6 Table 3 adds eight accuracy entries. For example, raw-event probing yields 35.52% on DVS Gesture and 12.65% on ASL-DVS, versus 56.32% and 38.90% using the proposed embeddings alone. The previous five-layer probing results, 86.94% and 69.83%, are retained. Main benchmark and efficiency values remain unchanged, although the stated ASL-DVS event count changes; no same-setting performance gain is established.

T1.justification: Appendix A.5 corrects inverse fusion from division by rho to division by log(rho)+1, matching the forward formula. Appendix A.1 removes the triangle-inequality rationale for the retained incremental minimum-distance update. The Taylor argument is essentially unchanged. The revised temporal definition introduces t/max(t), which does not generally support the retained absolute-time-shift-invariance claim because the denominator changes under a shift.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction remove the categorical claim that Event2Vec resolves the sparsity/GPU-efficiency conflict for the first time. V6 instead presents empirical support for efficient Transformer processing of events. The principal representation, efficiency, accuracy, and robustness contributions remain.

C2.justification: Appendix A.3 replaces the interpretation of attention-related degradation as negligible with a preference for FoX on harder long-sequence tasks, consistent with the retained DVS-Lip scores of 75.88% versus 72.35%. Section 4.2 also replaces 'minimal latency' with latency comparable to the fastest setting: batched K-Means++ takes 17.10 ms versus 15.95 ms for Faiss with 20 iterations.

D1.justification: The implementation recipe is substantially expanded and corrected across Sections 3.2–3.6 and Appendices A.1, A.2, A.5, and A.9. Changes include explicit coordinate normalization, sampling without replacement, cluster-count clipping, timestamp restoration, per-GPU batch and learning-rate definitions, attention normalization, masking construction, and augmentation formulas. These materially affect reproducibility. Hardware and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 only lists EventNet among point-based approaches. V6 Sections 3.2 and 3.5 explicitly acknowledge shared finite-address lookup and spatial/temporal factorization, then distinguish learned temporal encoding, neighborhood-aware spatial embeddings, intensity weighting, and GPU-oriented Transformer processing. This substantially revises positioning relative to a relevant precursor. Reference-list edits otherwise mainly correct metadata and consolidate duplicate BERT entries.

P1.justification: V6 condenses the abstract, removes a repetitive introduction paragraph, clarifies method and appendix prose, and standardizes terminology. 'Linear Attention + Event2Vec' becomes 'Transformer + Event2Vec,' consistent with the already described FoX backbone. The overall section and appendix organization remains.

P2.justification: The architecture diagram moves from v4 Figure 6 in the appendix to v6 Figure 2 in the main text, with rearranged panels and a corrected temporal-input label. V6 adds the linear-probing table and relocates the retained ablation tables. Existing plots are resized or regrouped, particularly appendix Figures 7–9, while their underlying results are retained.

improvement.justification: V6 improves attribution through its EventNet comparison, strengthens interpretation through the added probing controls, and corrects important reproducibility and inverse-fusion errors. These support a limited overall quality gain. The benchmark evidence is largely retained, and the PDFs do not establish reruns under the revised settings. The new timestamp normalization also leaves the time-shift-invariance claim mathematically unsupported without an additional assumption.
